sources.entry: Alpaca - Developed by Stanford, Alpaca is an instruction-following model based on LLaMA, fine-tuned for improved performance on specific tasks. Alpaca can be deployed locally, allowing researchers to work with large language models offline for greater privacy and control.

summary.name: Alpaca
summary.one_liner: Alpaca is a Stanford CRFM instruction-following language model fine-tuned from Meta's LLaMA 7B on 52K instruction demonstrations generated with OpenAI's text-davinci-003.
use_cases: reproducing a small instruction-tuned LLM cheaply
studying hallucination and safety failures in LLMs
running a language model locally or offline
summary.what_it_does: The page announces Alpaca 7B, a model fine-tuned from LLaMA 7B using supervised learning on 52K instruction-following demonstrations generated with text-davinci-003 via a self-instruct style pipeline. The authors report that in a blind pairwise human evaluation on the self-instruct evaluation set, Alpaca performed similarly to text-davinci-003 (90 wins versus 89). They released the training recipe, the data, the data generation code, and training code based on the Hugging Face API. The authors also state they intended to release model weights later. The page documents known limitations, including hallucination, toxicity and stereotypes.
notable: Fine-tuned from Meta's LLaMA 7B on 52K instruction demonstrations, with training reported under $600 total cost
Blog-reported blind evaluation roughly matched text-davinci-003 on the self-instruct evaluation set
Outputs watermarked using the Kirchenbauer et al. 2023 method to help detect Alpaca-generated text
caveats: Intended only for academic research; commercial use is prohibited due to LLaMA's non-commercial license and OpenAI's terms
Public demo has been disabled per the page update
Model weights were not yet released at the time of the post; only the recipe, data and code were released
Not designed with adequate safety measures and not ready for general deployment; prone to hallucination
